newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina OKs foreign funds with Mercosur assets.
newsitem.headline: Argentina OKs foreign funds with Mercosur assets.

text.p: Argentina's Securities and Exchange Commission (CNV) said Thursday it has approved the sale of foreign investment funds in the local market.

But the CNV said it will only let funds operate here if they observe the current requirement that at least 75 percent of their portfolio be in instruments issued in Argentina or its Mercosur partners Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
The CNV said in a statement it had decided to authorize trading in foreign funds because "foreign institutions have shown interest in developing these activities" in Argentina.

"This is good news for international funds," said a local fund manager. "Before, they would not authorize foreign funds to trade and now they will, but sticking to the requirement of 75 percent in the Mercosur.
"That limits the impact of the change," he said.
